overview.headline: How the 1803 Louisiana purchase doubled the nation and deepened divisions

keyPoints.point: Students learn the United States purchased 828,000 square miles west of the Mississippi River for $15 million.
keyPoints.quote: the United States purchased 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River for $15 million

keyPoints.point: Students learn negotiators were authorized to pay up to $10 million for New Orleans and the Floridas before being offered Louisiana.
keyPoints.quote: were authorized to pay France up to $10 million solely for the port of New Orleans and the Floridas

keyPoints.point: Students learn President Thomas Jefferson set aside strict constitutional doubts to expand across the continent.
keyPoints.quote: the desire to expand the United States across the entire continent trumped his ideological beliefs

keyPoints.point: Students learn expansion exposed sectional weaknesses over slavery leading to compromises and civil war.
keyPoints.quote: also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South, especially related to the issue of slavery

keyPoints.point: Students learn the purchase ignored Native peoples who were later forced onto reservations and lost tribal lands.
keyPoints.quote: Ultimately, Native people were forcibly moved on to reservations, losing vast acreage of their tribal lands

keyTerms.gloss: 1803 transaction that ignored Native presence while doubling the nation's size
keyTerms.quote: In addition, the Louisiana Purchase ignored the potential impact on Native Americans.

keyTerms.gloss: Port city negotiators were originally authorized to obtain for up to $10 million
keyTerms.quote: were authorized to pay France up to $10 million solely for the port of New Orleans and the Floridas

keyTerms.gloss: Belief that the Constitution must be read in a strict way that limits government authority
keyTerms.quote: President Thomas Jefferson was generally a strict interpreter of the Constitution who wondered

keyTerms.gloss: Divisions between North and South exposed by expansion over slavery
keyTerms.quote: also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South, especially related to the issue of slavery

keyTerms.gloss: Compromise that tried to maintain balance between free and slave states
keyTerms.quote: (notably the Missouri Compromise and the Compromise of 1850)

keyTerms.gloss: Thousands of tribal members populated the ceded lands before removal
keyTerms.quote: was populated with thousands of American Indians across dozens of tribes
